problem: Existing VLN benchmarks (R2R, VLN-CE) are episodic: agent memory is wiped before every instruction, so they never test cold-start-free, persistent-environment navigation as in deployed robots, and they give no incentive to build maps or memory.
motivation: Deployed robots stay in the same space for long periods and should use past experience (e.g., previously seen rooms) to follow future instructions. The authors observe that chaining R2R episodes into tours quickly covers the scene: after 10 episodes over 50% of the next target path and over 70% of the tour region has been observed.
key_idea: Define Iterative VLN (IVLN), where an agent follows an ordered tour of up to 100 R2R instructions in one scene while retaining memory across episodes (with oracle teleportation between episodes), and evaluate it with a tour-level t-nDTW metric.
insight: Extending unstructured implicit memory (history tokens in HAMT, GRU state in CMA) does not exploit tours and often hurts, whereas explicit semantic/occupancy maps built iteratively improve results. Map agents evaluated with iterative maps beat episodic-map evaluation, most strongly when trained with iterative maps (+3-4 t-nDTW, rows 4 vs 5 and 13 vs 14 of the map table). Known (pre-explored) maps do not beat iteratively built maps, and inferred semantics cost only about 1 t-nDTW.
method: Tour generation: for each R2R split and scene, partition paths into inter-navigable sets via geodesic distance (nav graph or navmesh), then order them by approximately solving an asymmetric TSP with Lin-Kernighan (LKH) to minimize oracle travel; tours are duplicated per instruction when multiple instructions exist per path.

Iterative paradigm: an agent navigation phase (follow the instruction until STOP or the step limit), then an oracle phase that guides the agent to the goal if it is not within 0.5 m and then to the next episode's start, while the agent passively observes.

t-nDTW metric: nDTW computed over the concatenated tour paths with infinite cost between points of different episodes (no credit for following the wrong instruction), aggregated across tours weighted by episode count.
TourHAMT (IVLN): HAMT whose history includes state-action pairs from previous episodes (last 50 steps) with a PREV separator token, an unfrozen history encoder, and inflection weighting.

Tour-memory CMA variants (IVLN-CE): TourCMA (vision GRU reset per tour), PoolCMA (episodic GRU plus a max-pooled tour vector), PoolEndCMA (tour vector concatenated with the final state); trained with truncated BPTT at episode boundaries.

MAP-CMA: builds a top-down 64x64 map of occupancy plus 13 semantic classes (ground-truth or RedNet-predicted) by unprojecting depth; a CoBRA conv encoder replaces the RGB features in CMA; trained with teacher forcing on EnvDrop then DAgger, using episodic, iterative, or known maps at train and eval (18 settings).

setting.backbone: HAMT / TourHAMT (transformer, fine-tuned from pretrained HAMT); CMA, TourCMA, PoolCMA, PoolEndCMA (GRU, trained from scratch); MAP-CMA (CMA with map encoder, plus RedNet for semantics)
setting.training_data: IVLN / IVLN-CE Train tours built from R2R / R2R-CE (14,025 and 10,668 episodes); MAP-CMA also uses EnvDrop augmentation ported to CE and DAgger; RedNet fine-tuned for semantics
setting.observation: IVLN: panoramic RGB views on the nav graph; IVLN-CE: egocentric RGB-D (CMA uses depth); MAP-CMA uses depth-derived semantic/occupancy maps
setting.action_space: IVLN: discrete nav-graph viewpoints; IVLN-CE: low-level TURN-LEFT/TURN-RIGHT/MOVE-FORWARD/STOP
setting.privileged: Oracle guidance between episodes (teleport to goal and next start) is part of the task; ground-truth semantics/occupancy and known (pre-explored) maps are used in some analysis rows

numbers_note: Table cells were transcribed as printed. Val-Seen results exist for all rows but are omitted here. IVLN and IVLN-CE are not in the canonical list, so they are labeled other:. Tables 1-2 give mean over 3 runs (± std error dropped in the metrics); the map table has no error bars. The appendix reports 48 t-nDTW, 36 SR and 33 SPL for the best MAP-CMA on the regenerated tip-to-tip Val-Unseen split.
results: Unstructured memory fails: TourHAMT reaches t-nDTW 32 vs 50 for episodic HAMT on IVLN Val-Unseen, and the CMA tour variants match but do not beat CMA (about 36-38 vs 38). Iterative-map MAP-CMA reaches t-nDTW 47-48 on IVLN-CE Val-Unseen, about +9 over CMA (though DAgger training is a confound), and iterative maps beat episodic maps at eval.
limitations: Only English instructions in staged, lavish indoor scenes.
Comparison of MAP-CMA vs CMA is confounded by DAgger fine-tuning used only for map agents.
Absolute performance is low (episodic SPL 32 vs 76 for humans), and the test leaderboard needs a modified oracle phase with tip-to-tip tour ordering.
